fact: A nearby red dwarf with a planet — and a target of a deliberate message to the stars.
bio: Luyten's Star is a red dwarf about 12.4 light-years away in Canis Minor, not far in our sky from bright Procyon. It hosts a planetary system including a super-Earth in its habitable zone — a world so nearby that it has been chosen as a target for interstellar radio messages sent from Earth.
cultural: It is named for Willem Jacob Luyten, the astronomer who catalogued the motions of thousands of faint high-velocity stars in the 20th century. Its planet's proximity has made it a focus of both exoplanet study and speculation about contact.
